newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mostly steady on Friday in limited activity as dealers watch the declining trend in CBOT corn and soybean prices.
"Very limited trading is going on. There are few buyers coming in here and there," a Minneapolis dealer said.

He noted some of the buyers' needs have already been covered. "I know people are delaying shipments," he said. "Some of the feed mixers do not need to buy anything for the nearbys. Next week, we will see better demand."
He expects farmers to hold on to their stocks waiting for better corn prices. "We might see a recovery, he said.
Another dealer agreed, adding the market would like to see corn and bean prices stabilize, particularly after this week.
"The guy who has been buying hand-to-mouth has been right, and we all have that tendency to be doing what has been working. So there is very little forward contracting," he said.
"It's a pretty dull today," a Carolinas dealer said. "People are surprised how cheap the markets are. Corn, beans and soymeal fell so much yesterday (Thursday)." The market was "stunned," he said.
But in the Northeast, nearby supplies remained tight.

"There is still no weekend (mill) run time, which makes nearby supplies tight," a Buffalo dealer said. "Next week is just about sold out. There is a spot load here and there but you have to hunt for it."
